title: Don't Be Chutney on the Stand
subtitle: AI judgment, hallucinations, and why polished output still needs receipts.
lesson: How to check, challenge, source, and contain AI output when it sounds confident but may be wrong, missing context, or not relevant to the real work.
emotionalBeat: First betrayal: AI sounded certain, she caught it, and now she trusts herself more.
oneLineDescription: The one in which she gets a Regina George-confident answer, catches the Chutney detail, and checks the timeline before it borrows her name.
episodeDescription: The one in which AI sounds polished enough to use, the Burn Book explains why confidence is not evidence, and Elle Woods becomes the verification model: claim, timeline, domain knowledge, contradiction, receipts.
previously: She learned that prompting is delegation: tell AI what you want, what you really really want.
tryOn: Use a low-risk work task or source notes, run Prompt Like Elle in your own AI tool, then verify at least three claims before using it.
mainCharacterEnergy: I can use the draft. I still check the alibi.
rememberLine: AI can write like Regina George. You still need to check like Elle Woods.
communityPrompt: What is the most confident wrong AI answer you have seen? Share the lesson, not confidential workplace details.
